cancellationPolicy:
Refund Policy

At Grand Bay of the Sea, we aim to provide memorable diving experiences while maintaining fairness in our policies. Please review our refund policy below:

Cancellations by the Customer:

More than 7 days before the scheduled activity (excluding diving courses): Full refund or rescheduling at no additional cost.7 days to 48 hours before the scheduled activity (excluding diving courses): 50% refund or the option to reschedule.Less than 48 hours before the scheduled activity: No refund will be issued.

Diving Courses:

Payments for diving courses are non-refundable. Rescheduling may be possible under certain circumstances. Please contact us for more details.

Cancellations by Grand Bay of the Sea:

If we cancel your activity due to unforeseen circumstances (e.g., weather, equipment issues), you will have the option to reschedule or receive a full refund for eligible activities. This does not apply to diving courses.

Special Considerations:

Refunds for multi-day packages will be prorated based on unused portions of the package (excluding diving courses).Medical or personal emergencies will be handled on a case-by-case basis, and supporting documentation may be required.

Refund Process:

Refund requests must be submitted in writing to grandbayofthesea@gmail.com

diveSites.name: El Nino
diveSites.summary: One of our favourite first-ocean-dive sites: shallow, calm and clear, with vibrant schools of tropical fish. Ideal after a Discover Scuba session.

diveSites.name: Finger Coral Plantation
diveSites.summary: Home to our coral nursery, where young fragments grow before being transplanted onto the reef. Shallow and easy, with yellowtail snappers everywhere.

diveSites.name: Submarine
diveSites.summary: A Russian tourist submarine that sank off Cabeza de Toro in 1998 — one of Punta Cana's most unusual artificial reefs. Shallow, bright and beginner-friendly.

diveSites.name: Cuevitas
diveSites.summary: Sunlit swim-throughs and small caves, no overhead training needed. Watch for lobster and cleaner shrimp as sunbeams cut through the rock.

diveSites.name: Atlantic Princess - Bayahibe
diveSites.summary: A former cruise ship, now one of the best first wreck dives in the DR — shallow, full of character and covered in coral. On our Bayahibe trips.

diveSites.name: Park Reef
diveSites.summary: A calm, easy dive over coral-covered rock, reliably clear even when conditions elsewhere aren't. One of the best sites for turtles, lobster and squid.

diveSites.name: Wreck Monica
diveSites.summary: An 1880s French cargo ship that once carried materials for the Panama Canal. Propeller, engine and boiler are still visible — an easy first wreck dive.

diveSites.name: Rock City
diveSites.summary: Natural canyons in the reef feel like flying down underwater streets, walls covered in hard corals and sponges. A superb drift dive when conditions allow.

diveSites.name: Anchor
diveSites.summary: A healthy reef where the Monica's anchor chain still rests across the coral. A great step up for Open Water divers and a natural pairing with the wreck.

diveSites.name: Shark Point
diveSites.summary: An expansive coral garden on pristine deep reef and a prime spot for nurse and reef sharks — no cage, no bait. Needs Advanced Open Water or 20+ dives.

diveSites.name: The Wall - Catalina
diveSites.summary: A spectacular drop-off, arguably the best dive site in the DR. A coral-covered wall teeming with life, and the signature dive of our Catalina day trip.

diveSites.name: St. George Wreck - Bayahibe
diveSites.summary: A 73 m Scottish-built cargo ship sunk as an artificial reef, now home to barracuda, morays and groupers. A deep highlight of our Bayahibe day trips.

liveaboards.intro:
Explore the Dominican Republic's Most Spectacular Marine Environments

DIVE DEEPER WITH GRAND BAY OF THE SEA

Experience the ultimate Dominican Republic diving adventure with our exclusive liveaboard expeditions. Grand Bay of the Sea proudly offers premium multi-day journeys to the most pristine and rarely visited waters of the Dominican Republic. Leave the crowds behind and immerse yourself in extraordinary marine environments that can only be accessed by liveaboard vessel.Our professional crew, accommodations, and exceptional dining create the perfect setting for the underwater adventure of a lifetime. Whether you're seeking vibrant coral reefs at Silverbank or majestic humpback whales in Samana Bay, our liveaboard experiences deliver unforgettable memories.
liveaboards.silverBank:
Departing from Sosua - Available June, July & August

Journey to the legendary Silverbank, a remote underwater sanctuary on the northern coast of the Dominican Republic. During summer months, this protected marine reserve offers exceptional diving among pristine coral formations and abundant marine life rarely visited by other divers.
liveaboards.whaleWatching:
Los Haitises to Cayo Levantado - Prime Season Janurary-March

Embark on an extraordinary whale watching journey through Samana Bay's most magical waters. Starting from the lush mangroves and limestone formations of Los Haitises National Park and culminating at the idyllic Cayo Levantado (Bacardi Island), this expedition offers unparalleled opportunities to observe magnificent humpback whales in their natural environment.

faqs.a: The St. George is a 73-meter cargo ship originally built in Scotland in 1962. It was used to transport wheat and barley between Europe and the Caribbean before being intentionally sunk in 1999 to create an artificial reef. It now rests at 40 meters depth half a mile off the coast of Dominicus in Bayahibe and is home to barracudas, groupers, moray eels, and king mackerels. It is widely considered one of the best wreck dives in the Caribbean.
faqs.q: What is the St. George wreck in Bayahibe?
